Ordering half is confirmed. So the shorthand scan runs before the root-type check, as the claim says. Trace of the falsifying inputs through uses_table_shorthand (lines 79-121): comments are not tokens, so '/* c */ TABLE t' gives previous='' and returns True. A quoted or backticked `TABLE` is an IDENTIFIER token, not TokenType.TABLE, so it is not flagged, and it is not a shorthand either. A quoted identifier or string before TABLE resets previous to '' (119-120), so it cannot exempt one. The exempting predecessors ('.', CREATE, SHOW, EXPLAIN, ANALYZE and so on) cannot precede a real TABLE-t query operand; valid positions such as start, ';', '(', ')', UNION/ALL/DISTINCT and AS ( all return True. _mysql_parse_sql (477-534) only rewrites CR inside comments, so tokenizing the original SQL should match tokenizing the sanitized SQL on the supported >=30.22 tokenizers.
